sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialized Air/Sea Transport of Regulated Hazardous Chemicals

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BITs with the United States (2004), United Kingdom, Germany, China, and over 100 other countries; numerous DTAs and FTAs including with the EU member states and major trading partners

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF, Articles L561-1 to L561-46); Ordonnance n° 2017-1164 du 12 septembre 2017 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, as amended by Law n° 2019-486 du 22 mai 2019

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague Convention states) or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from UBO register or beneficial ownership declaration

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening against French, EU, UN, OFAC, and domestic lists; full compliance with CMF AML/CFT obligations including customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official language is French; company names must be in French or use authorized transliterations; English names permitted with French translation
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Geographical or political terms without consent
Words suggesting public utility or monopoly
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name rejected, administrative appeal to the President of the commercial court within 2 months of notification

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for standard SARL; however, for hazardous materials transport requiring specific licenses, effective management and substance requirements may necessitate a physical office or dedicated compliance setup
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium risk; authorities may conduct unannounced inspections to verify registered office and compliance with commercial substance rules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate lawyer fees for due diligence and incorporation documents
UBO registration and related compliance setup
Initial AML/CFT policy and screening setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (SARL formation and governance); Code des transports, Articles L. 1411-1 et seq. and L. 5111-1 et seq. (freight forwarding and dangerous goods transport licensing); Environmental Code, Articles L. 511-1 et seq. (ICPE regime); Décret n° 2021-1374 du 20 octobre 2021 (professional competence and financial guarantee for commissionnaires de transport)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated electronically by INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle); final registration on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's jurisdiction
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise (M0/S0 form) submitted via the Guichet Unique portal, accompanied by the signed Statuts (Articles of Association) and the annexes required for RCS registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum for an SARL; the capital is freely fixed in the Statuts. The capital must be fully subscribed by the associates, and cash contributions must be paid up to at least one-fifth (20%) at incorporation, with the balance due within five years. For dangerous goods forwarding, the transport licensing authority additionally requires a financial guarantee (garantie financière) covering the forwarder's civil liability, maintained for the duration of registration on the Registre des commissionnaires de transport.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: I. RESOLVED that the company approves the subscription by each founding member of the number of shares set opposite their respective names in the share register and that the capital is declared fully subscribed. II. RESOLVED that the registered office be fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Association, domiciled with the corporate service provider. III. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed Gérant (Manager) with full powers to act and bind the company within the corporate purpose. IV. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser under ADR Chapter 1.8.3. V. RESOLVED that the Gérant open bank accounts, file the incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique, and arrange legal publication. VI. RESOLVED that formation expenses be ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Signature of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founded associates acting jointly; notarization (acte notarié) is mandatory only if real property is contributed, otherwise a private deed (sous seing privé) suffices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, enumerating the corporate purpose including 'commission de transport et transit de marchandises dangereuses sous régime ADR/IMDG/IATA', the share capital, the division of shares, the share transfer rules, the empowerment and powers of the Gérant, the registered office address, and the duration of the company. Every page must be initialled and the final page signed by all associates; the Gérant's written acceptance of appointment must be annexed.
required_dossiers: Statuts signed by all associates (two original copies)
Acte de nomination du Gérant (appointment deed with signed acceptance)
Identity documents (passport or national ID) of each associate and the Gérant
Déclaration de non-condamnation (declaration of absence of personal bankruptcy / disqualification) for the Gérant
Certificat de capacité professionnelle or evidence thereof (for commissionnaire de transport registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Statuts are challenged by the registry or a third party, the associates may execute an 'acte rectificatif' (amending deed) or adopt a 'résolution complémentaire' at an extraordinary general meeting; any defect in the consent of an associate may be cured by a new signature page or judicial rectification under Article L. 210-7 of the Commercial Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Capital Account and Issuance of the Depositary Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A bank established in France or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-interest-bearing blocked account in the name of the SARL being formed and deposit the cash portion of the capital (at least 20% of the subscribed cash capital). The financial institution issues a 'certificat du dépositaire des fonds' (certificate of deposit) listing the depositor, the amount, and the account holder. The certificate is remitted to the founder and must be annexed to the incorporation filing. Funds are released to the Gérant automatically upon issuance of the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts and pro-forma Kbis request (attestation of future registration)
Identity documents of the founding associates and the Gérant
Certificate of deposit (certificat du dépositaire des fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account due to the high-risk DG forwarding activity, the founder may apply to the Banque de France under Article L. 312-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code for the right to an account ('droit au compte'); the bank must designate a credit institution within 10 days or the Banque de France appoints one.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Notice in a Legal Announcement Journal (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) approved for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the chosen JAL to publish the 'avis de constitution' containing the corporate name, legal form, capital, registered office, duration, corporate purpose, and names of the Gérant(s). Obtain the 'attestation de parution' (certificate of publication) from the journal; this certificate must be enclosed with the registration dossier. The publication must occur before submitting the incorporation application to the Guichet Unique.
required_dossiers: Copy of the Statuts (extract or full text for the advertisement)
Identity data confirming the corporate name availability (negative certificate of name search or Kbis lien verification)
Power of attorney if published through a legal-tech provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL discovers a conflict with an earlier registered corporate name, the publisher will refuse the announcement; the founders must amend the name by an act of 'changement de dénomination' and republish, ensuring the name is available through an INPI/Infogreffe name search prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Digital Submission of the Incorporation Dossier to the Guichet Unique (RCS Registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI; substantive legal review performed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet Unique portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), complete the M0/S0 declaration for a commercial SARL, upload the PDF Statuts, the certificate of capital deposit, the JAL publication attestation, the Gérant's appointment deed and identity documents, and pay the state filing fee of €24 (plus optional tax registration fees). The Greffe verifies legal regularity, and upon approval issues the 'extrait Kbis' with a SIRET number, which constitutes the company's birth certificate. All tax and social administration notifications are effected simultaneously via the unique portal.
required_dossiers: Completed M0/S0 online form
Two original signed copies of the Statuts (uploaded and original retained)
Certificat du dépositaire des fonds
Attestation de parution au JAL (legal publication certificate)
Acte de nomination du Gérant and declaration of non-conviction
Copies of identity documents of associates and managers
Declaration of the beneficial owner(s) (déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif) and supporting proof
Proof of domiciliation of the registered office (lease, free occupation agreement, or domiciliation contract)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a 'rejet' or 'récépissé de rejet motivé', the portal displays the precise legal deficiencies; the declarant must rectify and resubmit within the portal, generally without new fees for corrections within the same procedure. If the Greffe fails to act within the statutory delay, the applicant may apply to the President of the Commercial Court (référé) to request an order compelling registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social, and Customs Opening Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), URSSAF, and Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Kbis, the company is automatically assigned a SIRET and is pre-registered with URSSAF for employer charges. The Gérant must activate the corporate tax file at the SIE by filing a 'déclaration d'identification' and filing the first corporate income tax return; apply for a VAT number (intra-community VAT EU number) through the SIE online interface; and for the DG forwarding business, apply to the DGDDI for a customs guarantee (AEO or single guarantee) if customs clearance services are provided. Jointly, register the professional bank account (IBAN) for incoming Swift Wire transfers and Letter of Credit payments, and file the first 'déclaration de résultat' in accordance with the chosen accounting year.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis (proof of RCS registration)
Statuts and Gérant appointment deed
Corporate bank account certificate (RIB/IBAN)
VAT and corporate income tax registration forms via the SIE portal
Customs activity declaration (if acting as déclarant en douane)
Power of attorney if a tax agent or accountant acts on behalf of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SIE delays VAT issuance, the company may apply for a provisional VAT number under Article 286 of the CGI by submitting the Kbis and a sworn statement; if URSSAF fails to acknowledge the employer file, the director should invoke the 'sans réponse' procedure and obtain a formal acknowledgement by registered letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Dangerous Goods Forwarding Authorization Dossier (Professional Competence, Financial Guarantee, and Safety Adviser Nomination)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Infrastructures, des Transports et des Mobilités (DGITM) via the Registre des commissionnaires de transport platform, and DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) for the dangerous goods safety adviser approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for registration on the Registre des commissionnaires de transport by evidencing the professional competence certificate (certificat de capacité professionnelle) of the manager or of an employed competent person, and by providing a financial guarantee certificate issued by an approved bank or insurer covering the forwarder's liability (amount adapted to the projected annual handling volumes). In parallel, designate the internal 'conseiller à la sécurité' (Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser) holding a valid ADR 1.8.3 vocational training certificate issued by the Ministry, and notify the appointment to the DREAL of the registered office region. For installations involving storage or transshipment of dangerous products, file the ICPE declaration or request DREAL authorization as applicable.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis and proof of registered office
Certificat de capacité professionnelle (professional competence certificate) of the manager or nominated person
Financial guarantee certificate (garantie financière) from an approved credit institution or insurer
Certificate of the Internal Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser (attestation conseiller à la sécurité ADR)
DREAL notification form for the safety adviser
ICPE declaration or authorization application (if warehousing/transshipment of dangerous goods on site)
Proof of civil liability insurance covering DG forwarding operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended or refused, the applicant may provide the missing evidence within the suspension period indicated by the Register's decision; an appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Transport within two months, and ultimately before the Administrative Court (Tribunal administratif). If the financial guarantee is deemed insufficient, the company must increase the guarantee amount with its bank and re-submit the updated certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Infrastructures, des Transports et des Mobilités (DGITM) within the Ministry of Ecological Transition — Registre des commissionnaires de transport; DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) for ICPE, dangerous goods safety adviser approval, and environmental inspections
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as Commissionnaire de Transport (Registre des commissionnaires de transport) with mandatory professional competence certificate and financial guarantee; Appointment of an Internal Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser (Conseiller à la sécurité ADR 1.8.3); Optional AEO-C (Authorized Economic Operator – Customs) authorization from DGDDI

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) — Mission Évaluation Environnementale, acting as the competent environmental authority under French Environmental Code
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category varies by quantity: (i) Exempt for pure administrative/provisional operations with no fixed storage; (ii) ICPE 'Déclaration' (registration) for small transshipment facilities under threshold quantities (e.g., Rubrique 4430 for flammable products); (iii) Full EIA (étude d'impact) and 'Autorisation' required when dangerous goods storage exceeds high thresholds (Rubriques 4430/4510/4511) or creates significant risks to water or residential zones. A Minimum 'Notice' (examen au cas par cas) may precede the full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Environmental Code and applicable 'arrêtés ministériels': wastewater discharges respecting DCO ≤ 125 mg/L and DBO5 ≤ 25 mg/L before release to surface water; VOC emissions limited to 20 mg/Nm3 for exhaust air and 10 g/m2 of product for equipment (Directive 2010/75/EU, Annex 7); hazardous waste handled through tracer slips (BSDD — bordereau de suivi des déchets dangereux) with mandatory declaration in the ADEME 'Sirene' track-and-trace database; combustion equipment must respect NOx and SO2 thresholds under the ICPE operating permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local Commission de Sécurité (avis de la commission de sécurité) including verification of means of fire-fighting, 'permis de feu' for hot works, and emergency response plans under the 'Plan de Prévention des Risques' (Risks); structural load inspection by an approved technical control bureau (bureau de contrôle — SOCOTEC/Apave) confirming floor loading capacity for racked DG pallet storage; occupational health clearance by the service de prévention et de santé au travail (occupational medical service) including pre-employment medical fitness, ATEX zoning classification and certification of electrical equipment for explosive atmospheres; installation of gas and flammable liquid detection, lightning-protection conformity assessment, and submission of the internal emergency and security plan (Plan d'Opération Interne) to DREAL where required by the authorization.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — portal impots.gouv.fr. VAT registration for non-established operators is handled by the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). Customs and EORI matters are under Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), portal douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity with a French VAT obligation but no French establishment must file an application for French VAT identification with DGFiP, attaching: certificate of incorporation, foreign VAT number, proof of address and bank details, description of supplied services, and, if non-EU established, a formal commitment to appoint a French tax representative. DGFiP issues a VAT identification number with the 'FR' prefix. In parallel, the entity obtains an EORI number from DGDDI. If the foreign entity creates a French fixed establishment or operates through the SARL, the SARL must complete French company and establishment registration with the SIE and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply a check-the-box entity classification regime. A SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Limited income-tax passthrough treatment is possible only for certain qualifying small SARLs under Article 239 bis AA CGI where all shareholders are individuals and functional criteria are met. A French resident parent may elect tax consolidation under Article 223 A CGI for qualifying wholly-owned subsidiaries, and ATAD-based hybrid mismatch limitations apply to deny deductions in defined cross-border cases.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 91,900 of annual turnover excluding tax for sales of goods and EUR 36,800 for services under the VAT franchise regime, with stepped lower thresholds; for DG freight-forwarding services, the relevant general threshold is EUR 36,800, but B2B supplies may trigger separate registration obligations where France is the place of supply absent an exempt threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing is being rolled out by DGFiP from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs, using structured formats (Factur-X / UBL) transmitted through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or certified dematerialization platforms (PDPs). Cross-border e-reporting to DGFiP is mandatory for B2B and B2C data. France does not use transactional digital stamping or per-invoice real-time fiscal clearance, but all relevant payments and invoice data must remain accessible for automated inspections and the statutory accounting file (Fichier des Écritures Comptables).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union qualify for 0% VAT exemption provided the goods physically leave French/EU customs territory and the supplier receives and retains documentary proof of export within the statutory period. For DG freight-forwarding services, transports directly tied to exported dangerous goods can qualify under the ancillary export service criteria if the service is supplied to the exporter and the existence of the export is duly evidenced.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / SAD lodged via DGDDI Delta), showing tax status 'AT' for VAT exemption
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight, evidencing actual physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT wire / Letter of Credit record proving foreign buyer settlement and repatriation of export proceeds
Signed commercial invoice, packing list, and UN-certified Dangerous Goods Declaration (IMDG / IATA DGD) for regulated hazardous cargo
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may recharacterize an export zero-rating claim as taxable if the documentary bundle is incomplete or the goods are not shown to have left France/EU within the required time. A reassessment triggers VAT at 20% plus late interest (intérêt de retard), and, where intent or bad faith is established, penalty surcharges of 40% to 80% under Article 1729 CGI. Fraudulent abuse of export exemption or false customs declarations may lead to criminal penalties, including fines up to €50,000 and imprisonment, alongside retrospective clawback of refunded input VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for foreign-exchange policy, with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for prudential licensing and anti-money-laundering supervision, and with AMF (Autorité des Marchés Financiers) for market and ISDA-framework oversight; all powers are codified in the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions; France applies the EU Treaty's free movement of capital (TFEU Article 63) and has abolished administrative exchange-control authorization for transfers within and into the Eurozone. There is no prior-approval regime for foreign-currency purchases, foreign-currency account opening (USD/GBP/CHF/JPY), or dividend and profit repatriation, but France retains statistical balance-of-payments (BOP) verification: each resident undertaking settlement with a non-resident at or above EUR 12,500 must file a 'déclaration de règlement' with the Banque de France through its licensed bank. Profit remittance to a non-resident shareholder is legally unrestricted and subject only to a reduced withholding tax under the applicable tax treaty (default 25% domestic rate), plus the ordinary obligation to document the distribution with board minutes and audited financial statements. The practical barrier for a hazardous-goods freight forwarder is not convertibility but the bank's heightened AML/KYC and sanctions-compliance documentation required to open and maintain the operating accounts that clear the flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no export-proceeds surrender ratio, no mandatory conversion of foreign-currency export receipts, and no statutory deadline for the repatriation of export revenue; a French SARL may lawfully hold USD and other currency collections in a domestic foreign-currency account or convert them into EUR at times of its choosing. The only binding obligation is the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration for any transaction with a non-resident equal to or greater than EUR 12,500; this declaration is informational only and carries no conversion or surrender consequence, and in practice the bank executes the declaration on the client's behalf via its BOP reporting channel.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. / LCL S.A. (with Crédit Agricole Corporate & Investment Bank for letters of credit)
BPCE S.A. / Natixis S.A. (Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Épargne network)
CIC S.A. (Crédit Industriel et Commercial, Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for core high-risk DG operations and letter-of-credit rails; MEDIUM only for auxiliary multi-currency expense accounts. ACPR-licensed and EU-passported electronic money institutions operating in France (notably Qonto, Shine, and Revolut Business) may open EUR, GBP, and USD IBANs with fast onboarding, but their transaction-risk policies commonly exclude freight forwarders dealing in regulated hazardous chemicals and their platforms cannot issue or advise documentary letters of credit (MT700) or provide Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting with the level of evidential detail expected for a High_Risk_Special_License entity. Use an EMI strictly for low-value operating disbursements such as software, insurance, and local subcontractor expenses; the principal clearing, escrow, and trade-finance flows must remain on Tier-1 commercial bank rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under CMF Article L561-5 et seq., KYC identity verification may in principle be performed remotely using eIDAS-compliant electronic identification and video conferencing. In practice, however, the DG hazardous-materials classification (High_Risk_Special_License) triggers the bank's internal enhanced due diligence policy, which mandates (i) at least one physical in-person meeting between an authorized signatory or the legal representative and the bank's relationship manager at either the registered office of the SARL or the bank branch, and (ii) a compliance site visit to the company's premises or bonded warehouse verifying storage, handling, and transport of dangerous goods. If non-resident directors or shareholders hold more than 25% of the capital, the bank will additionally require notarized and apostilled copies of their identity documents, a bank reference letter from their home institution, and the notarized original or apostilled power of attorney granting signatory rights to the French resident manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: sector coding 'ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510' combined with the description 'dangerous goods / hazardous chemicals' automatically classifies the applicant in the bank's high-risk registry and generates an automatic hold on account opening before any KYC file is reviewed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract issued within the previous three months; certificate of registration as a freight forwarder and transport commissionnaire (commissionnaire de transport / transitaire) with the French Ministry of Transport registry; ADR, IMDG, and IATA-DGR certificates issued to the company and its trained dangerous-goods safety advisers; two years of audited or accountant-certified financial statements; a corporate organization chart with all direct and indirect shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners; and a written explanation of the business model, including the complete list of DG classes and UN numbers handled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: sanctions and embargo screening fails or generates a 'hit' because the DG freight routes involve French ports (Le Havre, Marseille-Fos, Dunkerque) with transshipment to Asia, the Middle East, or Africa, nearby persons or vessels appearing on EU/OFAC/UN sanctions lists or in the bank's adverse-media database.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening reports (World-Check, LexisNexis, or Dow Jones) for all legal entities, beneficial owners, directors, and counterparties; end-user certificates and end-use declarations from each consignee, confirming civil commercial use and prohibition of re-export to embargoed destinations; a route-by-route export control matrix listing permitted countries and prohibited destinations; copies of shipment-specific export declarations (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens) and customs confirmations; and a written written compliance policy committing the SARL to block any transaction touching sanctioned states or parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: beneficial-ownership concealment risk triggered by a non-resident parent company or Asian shareholder holding more than 25% of the SARL through a chain of intermediate entities, and absence of a clear, filed declaration of beneficial owners at the registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The Beneficial Owner Declaration (Déclaration du bénéficiaire effectif) properly filed at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés and reflected on the Kbis; personal identity documents and proof of address for each ultimate individual together with a notarized bank reference letter from the UBO's home bank; apostilled or legalized corporate registry extracts for every intermediate holding entity; and confirmation of Legal Entity Identifiers (LEIs) for each corporate entity in the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: transactional-risk red flag arising from the requested payment rails 'SWIFT Wire + Letter of Credit' with large-value MT103 and MT700 flows to high-risk trade counterparties, potentially interpreted as suspicious round-tripping, trade-based money laundering, or mis-invoicing in the hazmat sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete underlying trade documents for a sample of at least three transactions: signed freight-forwarding contracts or CMR/AWB/seaway bills, commercial invoices mapping to the intended payment amounts, packing lists, insurance certificates for dangerous goods with an rated insurer, and customs declarations; anti-money-laundering training certificates for the money-laundering reporting officer; and an internal controls document demonstrating the four-eyes principle for any outgoing wire or LC exceeding EUR 50,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital injection must be routed through SWIFT MT103 (or RTGS/EURO1 equivalent for EU-origin funds) from the parent's bank to the SARL's EUR-denominated French operational account using the full beneficiary IBAN (FR76 + BIC) and the remittance narrative stating 'CAPITAL INJECTION - direct investment - [entity name and SIREN number].' The French receiving bank records the transaction under the Banque de France balance-of-payments classification for direct investment (investissements directs) and files the mandatory statistical declaration if the amount is at least EUR 12,500; no ex-ante authorization is required for an inbound investment, but the bank will request a notarized shareholder resolution and the updated Kbis to verify the sender's authority. If the injection is denominated in a non-euro currency such as USD, the French bank converts the funds at its spot rate on value date and credits the EUR account, or alternatively the parent may wire through a EUR correspondent account to avoid conversion friction and reduce cost. Post-closing, the SARL must ensure that the share capital increase is filed at the registry within one month and reflected in the Kbis, and in 2025 the intra-group treasury documentation should also include a term-sheet or intercompany funding agreement to substantiate the remittance purpose for both the bank and tax authorities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for DG trade settlements is the SWIFT MT103 message sent via SWIFT gpi for end-to-end tracking and same-day credit, with the field 70 remittance information containing the invoice reference, UN-number or HS tariff code, and transport document number; for larger or riskier purchases the SARL must use commercial letters of credit issued as MT700 by its French bank and advised through a confirming bank at the overseas seller, with MT707 amendments and MT710/MT720 transfers as required under UCP600. The bank will require ISO 20022 XML CBPR+ message formats for all payments and will insist that each instruction carries a Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR) and a valid purpose code (e.g., TRDP for trade payables); for payments to shipping companies, freight agents, and overseas warehouses, the SARL should maintain a standing approval matrix with dual signatories. Settlement of LC drawings is confirmed against presentation of the full document set (commercial invoice, bill of lading, DG packing certificate, insurance certificate, and certificate of origin), and any payment to a sanctioned state or blocked party is absolutely prohibited under the compliance policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (change à terme) against EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF, accessible for tenors up to 12 months under the French bank's ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, restricted to hedging documented DG receivables and payables under the 'besoin réel' (real need) doctrine.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies without a French-cleared deliverable market (e.g., KRW, IDR, PHP, TWD, and certain African franc-zone synthetic trades), permitted for commercial purposes only and settled in EUR or USD on the fixing rate.

European plain vanilla FX Options (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP calls and puts) for asymmetric protection against adverse freight-rate or currency movements; barrier, exotic, and speculative option structures are prohibited for unregulated non-financial companies.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) and short-term FX swaps (change manuel) matching EUR-USD assets and liabilities when the SARL carries foreign-currency debt or long-dated DG contracts; each instrument requires an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, a Credit Support Annex (CSA), and a delegation of authority to the corporate treasurer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale n°2065-SD) including balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal year-end; for calendar-year SARLs, e-filing deadline is 15 May of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes 10% late-filing penalty plus 0.20% per month late-payment interest under Article 1728 CGI; intentional concealment may increase penalty to 80% and subject directors to personal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) including balance sheet, income statement, and notes, filed with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) within the court's territorial competence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval must occur within six months of fiscal year-end; filing with the Greffe must occur within one month after approval; calendar-year SARLs typically file by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file exposes directors to civil fines up to €1,500, court-ordered injunctions, and eventual radiation du RCS (administrative strike-off) after continued non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business property contribution return (CFE n°1327-CFE) detailing premises and equipment subject to Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Local Tax Office (Pôle de Recouvrement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return due on or before 2 December for the current fiscal year; tax calculated from the rental value of premises used for business activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid CFE triggers 10% late-payment penalty, 0.20% monthly late interest, and enforced debt collection; continued non-payment does not directly cause strike-off but leads to tax liens and attachment measures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) applies to SARLs exceeding at least two of the following three thresholds: balance-sheet total €4,000,000, net turnover €8,000,000, or average workforce of 50 employees; also mandatory if the SARL controls or is controlled by another entity included in consolidated oversight under Articles L821-32 and L233-3 of the Commercial Code
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts must be prepared under French generally accepted accounting principles (PCG) as set by ANC Regulation 2016-07 (Plan Comptable Général), consistent with Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated accounts if the group is listed on a regulated market

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France imposes no standalone annual UBO confirmation form; the beneficial-owner (bénéficiaires effectifs) declaration is filed at incorporation and must be updated with the Greffe within 30 days after any share-transfer transaction that changes direct or indirect control thresholds of 25% of capital or voting rights; non-reporting carries criminal penalties of €7,500 and six months’ imprisonment
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des associés) including share transfers
Register of Directors (registre des dirigeants) with identity and powers
Minute Book (registre des procès-verbaux) of shareholders' and managers' decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 700–1,900 typical annual fee range for full-service registered-office/secretarial agent in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 8,000–24,000 typical certified audit fee range for a mid-market SARL triggering statutory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard (France: 25% corporate income tax rate from 2022; reduced 15% rate for small businesses on first €42,500 of profit under certain conditions)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €42,500 of taxable profit (subject to turnover ≤ €10m and paid-up capital conditions); R&D tax credit (CIR) 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to €100m, 5% above; young innovative company (JEI) exemptions; competitiveness and employment tax credit provisions; tax credits for energy transition (C2E) etc.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (déclaration de résultat) or 2065-SD filed via EFI (Échange de Fichiers Informatisés) / impots.gouv.fr professional space (dématérialisation GIE / EDI-TDFC)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due by the second business day following 1 May of the year following the fiscal year (Art. 223(1) CGI); for fiscal year closing 31 Dec, usually by 3 May (or second working day after 1 May); if closing date other than 31 Dec, deadline is second working day following 1 May; extensions for electronic filing (up to 15 May or later for online filers)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result before offset of prior losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL shareholder must ensure the entity reports French-sourced income; tax result computed on French worldwide or territorial basis per branch allocation rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward to be offset against current-year profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate carryforward losses of prior 5 years (or up to 10 years where applicable); losses of foreign PEs may not be deducted from France-sourced income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provision entries for litigation, bad debts, and DG transport insurance contingencies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provisions must be justified by objective facts as of closing; non-deductible provisions for fines and penalties added back

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065 / Section III (Intéressement, participation, and CICE complementary data)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a single-member SARL (EURL) operates in France, employee-related deductions require payroll compliance; non-resident managers do not alter deductible thresholds

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation schedules for specialized DG fleet equipment, tanks, and handling gear
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Portfolio of assets used in France must be booked in the French entity; fiscal depreciation applies per CGI Art. 39-1-2

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge (majoration) under Art. 1728 CGI, increased to 40% if an assessment notice was sent and filing is 30 days overdue, 80% for concealed activity; plus interest at statutory monthly rate (0.40% per month / 4.8% p.a., adjusted); €150 fixed penalty per omitted or inaccurate return (Art. 1728) and €15,000 (up to €20,000) for omitted statements; criminal penalties up to €75,000 and 5 years imprisonment for tax evasion (fraude fiscale)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory withholding of 25% (Art. 119bis-2 CGI) at time of dividend payment to non-resident parent, subject to exemption/relief under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; final withholding rate 12.8% for EU-domiciled corporate shareholders where conditions met
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the France–home DTA: (i) submit a validated Form 5000 / Form 5001 (attestation de résidence fiscale) or obtain a French Tax Residency Certificate (CRF) from the foreign jurisdiction; (ii) file with the French paying company; (iii) apply reduced rate or exemption before payment via a tax clearance (quitus fiscal); if withholding already levied, claim reimbursement via Form 5002 (réclamation) within the statutory period generally by 31 December of the second year following the credit year; for EU entities, offer compliance via the EU Savings Directive or double-tax relief clearing under CGI Art. 182B; require beneficial ownership proof and no artificial conduit arrangements per DTA Art. 29 and the Multilateral Instrument (MLI) principal purpose test
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties: 33.33% (Art. 182-1(b) CGI) for patents/ IP; treaty-reduced rates commonly 0–5% for royalties under OECD DTAs (e.g., Germany 0%, UK 0%, US 5% for industrial/commercial/scientific equipment and 5% for patent royalties); statutory WHT on interest: 0% for certain public debt and 12% on other bonds, often reduced to 0% under DTAs and EU Interest-Royalty Directive (where borrower and lender are EU associated companies); interest paid to non-resident parent under thin-capitalisation rules may be recharacterized as dividends and subjected to 25% WHT if the 1.5:1 debt/equity safe harbour is exceeded

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Multinational groups with headcount > 50 employees (or >400 for SME thresholds) and French turnover/ balance-sheet above €50 million (consolidated > €400m and >50 employees triggers Master/ Local File); local TP documentation (documentation de prix de transfert) mandatory under Art. L.13 AA of the LPF when the French entity exceeds €50m of transactions with related parties or €400m consolidated turnover or headcount above 50 (Form 2257 filing threshold: related-party transactions > or accounts > €50m); specifically Form 2257 (TP declaration) must be filed by entities with annual related-party turnover/gross assets above €50 million or group headcount above 50
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Profit Split Method (Profit-Split, incl. transactional and global accretion under OECD 2022 Pillar One context)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone ESR (Economic Substance Regulations) regime akin to UAE/DIFC; however, the doctrine of substance-over-form (substance prévaut sur la forme) plus Art. 1655 bis (abuse of law, abus de droit) require real economic activity; DG forwarding SARL must demonstrate actual dispatch centres, qualified ADR/DGSA (Transport of Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser) employment, dedicated hazmat warehousing and transport licences, and corporate substance; artificial arrangements lacking local decision-making trigger the GAAR (Art. L.64 LPF), the anti-artificial-arrangements doctrine, and can lead to recharacterization and 80% penalty plus 5-year criminal exposure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing DG invoices, under-declaring ADR premium revenue, fictitious cross-border invoicing for hazardous cargo, or failing to file the Form 2065 with intentional misstatement of turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties under Art. 1729 CGI: 40% majoration if bad faith, 80% if abus de droit or dissimulation of activity; criminal conviction under Art. 1741 CGI: up to €1,000,000 (increased to €2,000,000 if using bank accounts abroad) and prison up to 7 years (formerly 5), extended to 10 years for organised group
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director (gérant) personally liable to tax administration for civil restitution of evaded tax, penalties and interest; criminal exposure includes travel bans and detention; supervisory board members can face joint liability; mises en demeure and mise en jeu de la responsabilité civile of Court of Cassation (Cass. crim. 2019) pierces the veil for fraudulent concealment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the French SARL as a letterbox entity with no decision-making in France, booking freight margins in a low-tax jurisdiction and only nominal local DG licence holding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of profits under Art. 1655 bis CGI (abus de droit) and Art. L.64 LPF: 80% penalty on restated income plus late interest; denial of treaty benefits under MLI principal-purpose test; potential nullity of a licence under the Code du transport (regulatory suspension of the DG forwarding licence)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil restitution of reassessed tax plus penalties; director travel bans through judicial control (interdiction de quitter le territoire) in money-laundering-linked proceedings; imprisonment of the gérant up to 7 years when abuse of law is characterized as tax evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash or unverified third-party payments on high-risk DG corridors, orchestrating layered Swift wire transfers and invoices through shell pass-through entities to disguise underlying hazmat cargo and sanctions-related counterparties (e.g., OFAC-listed transshipment)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 324-1 et seq. French Criminal Code: up to 10 years imprisonment and €750,000 fine (or half the value of laundered funds if higher); Tracfin declarations for cash transactions ≥ €10,000; DG forwarding licence suspension and DNA-Type (Direction de la surveillance du territoire) scrutiny; asset freezing and confiscation under Art. 131-21 Penal Code
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and compliance officer face personal criminal liability; corporate veil lifting under Cass. crim. 2018; travel bans, freezing of personal bank accounts, and disqualification from professional forwarding activity for up to 10 years; statutory emergency custodial measure for hiding assets: additional 3 years imprisonment
